servinfo.title: Air Bleeding of Clutch System

item.ptxt: Brake fluid is extremely damaging to painted surfaces.
If brake fluid contacts painted surfaces, immediately wipe it off and flush the surfaces with water thoroughly.
If the clutch pedal is pumped continuously to bleed the clutch system, the oil seal of the operating cylinder may be damaged, resulting in fluid leakage.
After releasing the clutch pedal, wait at least 1 second before depressing it again.

servinfo.ptxt: Bleed hydraulic clutch system of air as follows whenever air enters hydraulic clutch system.

s1.ptxt: Fill master cylinder reservoir with brake fluid and keep the reservoir at least one-half full of fluid during bleeding operation.

sdm1.sdm-value: Refer to brake fluid reservoir cap.

s1.ptxt: Remove bleeder plug cap. Attach a vinyl tube (1) to bleeder plug, and insert the other end into container (2).
Depress clutch pedal several times, and then while holding it depressed, loosen bleeder plug about one-half a turn.
When fluid pressure in cylinder is completely released, retighten bleeder plug.
Repeat Step 3) – 4) until there are no more air bubbles in hydraulic line.
When air bubbles disappear from fluid flowing into container, hold clutch pedal depressed, and tighten bleeder plug.
After completing bleeding operation, apply fluid pressure to clutch line and check for leakage.
Replenish master cylinder reservoir with fluid up to specified level.
Check clutch pedal for operation. If spongy condition is felt, repeat entire procedure of bleeding.
